samples.question: The picture shows four lanes side by side. At the top, each lane holds one coloured bar; the four bars are red, blue, green and purple and every bar has its own height. Below the bars a stack of black rungs is drawn. Apply the rungs one at a time in top-to-bottom order, as the grey arrow on the left shows. Each rung joins exactly two lanes: the two lanes its black bar reaches. A small orange square sits just outside one of the two ends of each rung; that end is the marked end. Applying a rung puts the taller of the two bars then standing in those two lanes into the marked end's lane and the shorter of them into the other lane; if they are already arranged that way, applying the rung changes nothing. Bars keep their colour and their height while they move, lanes that a rung does not join are untouched, and only the two lanes a rung reaches are affected. The teal triangle below the lanes marks the queried lane. After all the rungs have been applied in order, which coloured bar stands in the queried lane? Answer with one of: red, blue, green, purple.
